newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo '96 GDP fell 9pct in real terms - institute.
newsitem.headline: Yugo '96 GDP fell 9pct in real terms - institute.

text.p: Yugoslav gross domestic product (GDP) in 1996 dropped nine percent in real terms against the previous year despite its 76 percent rise in absolute figures, a Belgrade think-tank said on Tuesday.
"According to the official statistics, GDP last year was 68.15 billion dinars, up 76 percent on 1995," said Stojan Stamenkovic, leading economist of the Institute for Economic Sciences (IEN).
"But if the retail price growth is calculated, GDP last year dropped some nine percent on the previous year," he said presenting IEN's latest Monthly Analyses and Forecasts.
The average price increase in 1996 was 93 percent on the previous year.
According to the official statistics, which calculated GDP on the volume of industrial production, agriculture and other economic aggregates, GDP rose 5.8 percent last year.
Stamenkovic said the institute raised the issue of reality of statistical figures and adequate treatment of losses when calculating GDP.

"Yugoslav economy last year incurred a net loss of some 8.75 billion dinars, but according to the official data GDP rose and industrial output was up 7.5 percent compared to the previous year," he said.
"The paradox of our economy is that physical volume of production is growing while at the same time incurring high losses."
The real GDP drop in 1996 was not nine percent since some of it was carried over from previous years, IEN said.
"What we can say is that the real value of GDP in 1994 has not been exceeded either in 1995 or in 1996," he said. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
